summary: Joanna Macy (1929–2025) worked in religious studies, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. She studied at Wellesley College (~1946–1950) and Syracuse University (~1973–1978), and her students included Stephanie Kaza and Doug Kraft.

Joanne Punzo Waghorne studied at the University of Chicago (~1971–1976). A scholar of religious studies and Indology, she held posts at the University of Massachusetts Boston (1975–1983), Bowdoin College (1983–1985), UNC Chapel Hill (1987–2002), and Syracuse University (from 2002).

Joe Bransford Wilson specialized in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, earning a Ph.D. from the University of Virginia (1984) after studies at UW–Madison. He taught at Virginia (1981–1985) and UNC Wilmington (attested 1994–2001).

Joe Cribb studied at Queen Mary University of London (~1967–1970). A specialist in history, archaeology, Indology, and Central Asian studies, he served as Keeper of Coins and Medals at the British Museum (1970–2010) and led the Oriental Numismatic Society (2011–2018).

Joel Peter Brereton is an Indologist and religious studies scholar who studied under Stanley Insler in 1971. He held positions at the University of Missouri (1999–2000) and the University of Texas at Austin, where he became professor emeritus.
Joel Tatelman works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned his D.Phil. from the University of Oxford in 1996 under the supervision of Alexis Sanderson.
Joen Imai is a Buddhist studies scholar who has served as a professor at Shuchiin University (attested 2010 and 2026).

Joerg Tuske is an Indology and philosophy scholar. He held a post at the University of Cambridge (attested 1998) and served as an associate professor of philosophy at Salisbury University (attested 2013).

Joey Hung is a scholar in computational and Buddhist studies who attended the Hong Kong Academy for Performing Arts. He has held positions at Dharma Drum Institute of Liberal Arts and the Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies.
Jogendra Singh is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at Nava Nalanda Mahavihara under Uma Shankar Vyas.

Jogindra Nath Samaddar (1884–1929) studied at Presidency University and Bangabasi College. An Indologist and historian, he taught at Pramatha-Manmatha College, St. Columba's College, Patna College (from 1912), and Patna University (1923).

Johan Elverskog studied at UC Berkeley (B.A.) and Indiana University Bloomington (M.A.). A scholar of Central Asian, Buddhist, and religious studies, he held research positions before becoming Dedman Family Distinguished Professor at Southern Methodist University (~2002).

Johan Hendrik Caspar Kern (1833–1917) studied at Utrecht, Leiden, and under Albrecht Weber. An Indologist and linguist, he taught in Maastricht and Varanasi before serving as Chair of Sanskrit at Leiden University (1865–1903).
Johan Hendrik Kern (1867–1933) was a linguist who held academic posts at the University of Groningen (1901–1924) and Leiden University (1924–1933).

Johan Huizinga (1872–1945), a scholar of history, archaeology, Indology, and linguistics, studied at Groningen and Leiden, where he learned from J. H. C. Kern. He held professorships at Groningen (1905–1915) and Leiden (1914–1942).

Johann Andreas Schmeller (1785–1852) studied at the University of Munich (~1801–1803). He taught at the Bavarian Cadet Corps (~1815–1827), served as custodian at the Bavarian State Library (1829), and held a chair at Munich (1846).

Johann Caspar von Orelli (1787–1849) was a scholar of linguistics. He taught at the Cantonal School of Graubünden (~1814–1819), the Carolinum Zürich (~1819–1833), and the University of Zurich (~1833–1849).

Johann Christoph Adelung (1732–1806) studied at the University of Halle-Wittenberg (1752). A linguist, he served as a professor at Evangelisches Ratsgymnasium Erfurt (1758) and as head librarian at the Saxon State and University Library Dresden (1787).

Johann Friedrich Blumenbach (1752–1840) was an academic in history and archaeology who studied at the University of Jena (~1769–1772) and the University of Göttingen (~1772–1775). He spent his career on the faculty at Göttingen (~1776–1840).
Johann Friedrich Herbart (1776–1841) was a philosopher who studied at the University of Jena (~1794–1797). He held a post at the University of Göttingen (~1802–1809) and taught Eduard Röer.
